title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher
talk_summary: A two-hour first-principles workshop on LLM inference covering KV-cache memory growth, prefill/decode phases, the quality-latency-throughput tradeoff, model optimizations (quantization, GQA/MLA), and serving optimizations (paged attention, continuous batching, prefix caching, speculative decoding). It benchmarks vLLM vs SGLang and concludes vLLM is a safe default for standard workloads while SGLang wins 3-4x on agentic multi-turn workloads.

takeaways.technique: Prefix caching with radix tree for agentic loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hashing whole prompts (which misses on any edit), they use a radix tree to cache shared prompt prefixes across requests, so repeated system prompts and agent scaffolding skip recomputation.
takeaways.numbers: prefix caching: throughput up, TTFT down, KV usage vs users down

takeaways.technique: Engine choice matters more for agentic workloads than standard ones
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmarked vLLM vs SGLang on plain Q&A and on a two-turn agentic review loop; plain workloads were statistically identical, but agentic branching favored SGLang 3-4x.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we do proper this agentic branching then I think uh this HG lang is three to four times better
takeaways.numbers: SGLang 3-4x better on agentic branching; no statistical difference on standard shared-GPT workload

takeaways.technique: KV cache size math to bound context vs concurrency
takeaways.what_they_do: They compute KV bytes per token from layers, head dims, and KV heads, then derive max concurrent users = free GPU memory / KV per user, exposing a hard context-vs-concurrency tradeoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is always a tradeoff between what context length you can serve versus how much cost you can save

takeaways.what_they_do: Quantizing the KV cache (not just weights) shrinks per-token memory so more tokens/users fit, with roughly unchanged throughput and latency in their benchmark.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your KV usage actually goes down. And this is because like you have quantized your key value space
takeaways.numbers: throughput/TTFT/latency approximately same; KV usage down

takeaways.technique: Weight quantization for fitting bigger models cheaper
takeaways.what_they_do: Compress BF16 weights to FP8/INT8/INT4/NF4 to fit larger models on smaller/cheaper GPUs, validating quality on external benchmarks rather than assuming no loss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of compressing it a floating point 16 we can apply different techniques like int 8 or int4 or nf4

takeaways.technique: Benchmark on your own workload shape, not generic prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: They ran two benchmark suites: a generic shared-GPT Q&A set and a custom two-turn agentic review loop, and got different conclusions from each.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you do it uh you may get different results
